question: E2 condition map: in each situational condition of the Thomas-Kilmann model, operationalized as one environment knob moved from the E1 base, which strategy pays best, for whom and at what cost in tokens and moves?

instances.note: shared by every condition; disjoint from the dev and E1 seeds

cells: the diagonal, every strategy against neutral and against competing in both seats: 24 cells, 480 games per condition
analysis: per condition: best strategy in symmetric play, against neutral and against competing, by points and by net payoff (points minus lambda x tokens/1000) for lambda swept from 0 to 20; regret of every strategy against the best in its condition; the lambda at which the best strategy changes

base.model_condition: the E1 regime, replayed on the shared E2 instances

urgent.prediction: fast closers win: competing against neutral, accommodating otherwise; collaborating loses most; agreement falls

time_cost.prediction: like urgent; avoiding and accommodating gain relative to the base; competing pairs pay the most in move costs

tight_budget.model_condition: confrontation costs more than it yields (avoiding's condition), as a reply-token budget
tight_budget.prediction: avoiding and accommodating are the best net strategies; collaborating is the worst; the ranking by raw points changes little

distributive.model_condition: conflicting goals, nothing to trade (compromising's condition)
distributive.prediction: collaborating equals compromising; competing exploits the soft strategies most

integrative.model_condition: complex problem that needs both perspectives (collaborating's condition)
integrative.prediction: collaborating beats compromising by the largest margin, in own and joint payoff

all_contested.prediction: more impasses under competing; compromising's relative standing improves

low_stakes_p2.model_condition: the issue matters more to the other side (accommodating's condition for the low-stakes side)
low_stakes_p2.prediction: the low-stakes side does best by accommodating and worst by competing; the high-stakes side does best by competing

power_p1.prediction: the strong side does best by competing, the weak side by compromising or accommodating; every pair gives the strong side more

open_info.model_condition: both sides see both sides' interests
open_info.prediction: collaborating's advantage over compromising shrinks and competing's exploitation of neutral shrinks
